::: {.profile-lead}
I teach and conduct research in quantitative finance and statistics at **Charles University in Prague**. I am also a **Visiting Professor at the Frankfurt School of Finance & Management**.
:::

My work connects financial prices, probability models, and portfolio choice. The [Likelihood Finance](likelihood/index.qmd) project develops this connection through concise explanations, interactive models, and links to the research behind them.

## Research

My research interests include portfolio theory, derivative pricing and hedging, stochastic processes, and prediction markets. A recurring question is what becomes simpler when a price is read as a likelihood ratio and an investment position as a probability distribution over future outcomes.

The interactive guide begins with the [binomial model](likelihood/binomial.qmd). It then follows the same structure through richer distributions, [utility and risk aversion](likelihood/utility.qmd), [mean–variance approximation](likelihood/mean-variance.qmd), and [option-implied measures](likelihood/options.qmd).

[Selected articles on this site](index.qmd#papers) provide entry points into the published work. Further research and professional profiles:

## Books

**[Principles of Portfolio Choice: An Information-Theoretic, Likelihood-Based Perspective](https://www.routledge.com/Principles-of-Portfolio-Choice-An-Information-Theoretic-Likelihood-Based-Perspective/Vecer/p/book/9781032951980)**, forthcoming from Chapman & Hall/CRC, develops portfolio selection through the correspondence between normalized payoffs and probability measures.

**[Stochastic Finance: A Numeraire Approach](https://www.routledge.com/Stochastic-Finance-A-Numeraire-Approach/Vecer/p/book/9781439812501)**, CRC Press, 2011, presents derivative valuation and hedging through relative prices and changes of numeraire.

## Academic background

I received my PhD in Mathematical Finance from **Carnegie Mellon University in 2000**. I was a faculty member in the Department of Statistics at **Columbia University from 2001 to 2010**, and Professor of Finance at the **Frankfurt School of Finance & Management from 2010 to 2015**, continuing there as a visiting professor since 2015.

My teaching has also included courses at the University of Michigan and Kyoto University. The [publisher's biography](https://www.routledge.com/Principles-of-Portfolio-Choice-An-Information-Theoretic-Likelihood-Based-Perspective/Vecer/p/book/9781032951980) gives further background on my academic and applied work.
